ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.

1.6. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
1.7. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.8. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.9. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.10. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.11. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.12. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.13. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.14. Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.15. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.16. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.17. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.18. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.19. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.20. Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.21. Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
1.22. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
3.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
3.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
4.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

5. Trip Cancellation
5.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
5.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
5.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

6. Emergency Medical Expenses
6.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
6.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
6.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
6.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
6.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
6.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.3. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.4. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.5. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

8. Making a claim
8.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3. You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

9. How to read this document
9.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
9.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
9.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

10. Premium payment
10.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
10.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

11. Currency
11.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
11.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

12. Data protection
12.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
12.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
12.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

13. Duty of fair presentation
13.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
13.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
13.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

14. Compensation scheme
14.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
14.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

15. Fraud
15.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
15.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

16. Emergency assistance
16.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
16.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
16.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

17. Changes in circumstances
17.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
17.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

18. Instalment agreements
18.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
18.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

19. Assignment
19.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

20. Personal liability
20.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
20.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
20.3. The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

21. Notices
21.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
21.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

22. Other insurance
22.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
22.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

23. Inflation
23.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
23.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

24. Cancellation
24.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
24.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
24.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

25. Environmental commitment
25.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
25.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

26. Payment of claims
26.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
26.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

27. Exchange of information
27.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
27.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

28. Communication
28.1. We will communicate with you in English.
28.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

29. Automatic renewal
29.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
29.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

30. Third-party administrators
30.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
30.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

31. Claims documents
31.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
31.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

32. Severability
32.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

33. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
33.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

34. Salvage
34.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
34.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

35. Complaints
35.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
35.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
35.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

36. Customer support
36.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
36.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

37. Records and evidence
37.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
37.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
37.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

38. Electronic documents
38.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
38.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
38.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

39. Arbitration
39.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
39.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

40. Sanctions
40.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

41. Waiver
41.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

42. Governing law
42.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
42.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

43. Accessibility
43.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

44. Interest
44.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

45. Reasonable precautions
45.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
45.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

1. Definitions
1.1. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.3. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.4. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.5. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
1.6. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.7. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Personal liability
3.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
3.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
3.3. The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

4. Market conditions
4.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
5.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

6. Rental car excess
6.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
6.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

7. Trip Cancellation
7.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
7.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
7.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
7.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
7.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

8. Emergency Medical Expenses
8.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
8.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
8.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
8.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
8.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
8.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

9. General exclusions
9.1. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
9.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

10. Making a claim
10.1. You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
10.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
10.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

11. Change of address
11.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
11.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

12. Changes in circumstances
12.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
12.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

13. Third-party administrators
13.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
13.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Customer (Luca): Hi, I need to make a claim on policy K431761 under Emergency Medical Expenses for emergency treatment for a cracked molar.
Agent: Sure. When did the policy start and what covers does your schedule show?
Customer (Luca): It started on Thursday, April 23, 2026. The schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, and extensions: none.
Agent: When did the incident happen, and what happened?
Customer (Luca): On Thursday, November 12, 2026. Luca's records show treatment for the same condition 8 months before the policy start date. Luca fell ill suddenly on the third day of the trip. The problem began while Luca was trekking at an altitude of 2,242 metres. The hospital report notes that Luca had not been drinking.
Agent: Anything else we should know?

Agent: Noted. I am logging this claim today, Saturday, February 13, 2027, the first time it has been reported to us. Our adjuster has assessed the loss at $475.

6.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.

7.5. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.6. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

39.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.

45.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Benefits Trust

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7. Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.9. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.10. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.11. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.12. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.13. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.14. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.15. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.16. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.19. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Currency
3.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
3.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

4. Records and evidence
4.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
4.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
4.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

5. Duty of fair presentation
5.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
5.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
5.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

6. Premium payment
6.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
6.2. If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

7. Leaving the plan
7.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
7.2. Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

8. Eligibility
8.1. Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
8.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

9. Optional cover: Hearing Care
9.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
9.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
9.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
9.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

10. Geographical limits
10.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
10.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

11. Compensation scheme
11.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
11.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

12. Environmental commitment
12.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
12.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

13. Joint policyholders
13.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
13.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

14. Changes in circumstances
14.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
14.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

15. Complaints
15.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
15.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
15.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

16. Cooperation
16.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
16.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

17. Waiver
17.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

18. Salvage
18.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
18.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

19. Change of address
19.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
19.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

20. Assignment
20.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

21. Data protection
21.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
21.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
21.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

22. Severability
22.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

23. Appeals
23.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
23.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
23.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

24. Other insurance
24.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
24.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

25. Discounts
25.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
25.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

26. Dental Care
26.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
26.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
26.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
26.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
26.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
26.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

27. Exchange of information
27.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
27.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

28. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
28.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

29. Coordination of benefits
29.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
29.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

30. Third-party administrators
30.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
30.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

31. Customer support
31.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
31.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

32. Sanctions
32.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

33. Therapy Services
33.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
33.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
33.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
33.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

34. Subrogation
34.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
34.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

35. Governing law
35.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
35.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

36. Taxes
36.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
36.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

37. Vision Care
37.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
37.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
37.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
37.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

38. How to read this document
38.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
38.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
38.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

39. Accessibility
39.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

40. Instalment agreements
40.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
40.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

41. Payment of claims
41.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
41.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

42. Renewal
42.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
42.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

43. Fraud
43.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
43.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

44. Cancellation
44.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
44.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
44.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

45. Interpretation
45.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
45.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
45.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

46. Market conditions
46.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

47. General exclusions
47.1. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
47.2. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
47.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
47.4. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

48. Electronic documents
48.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
48.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
48.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

49. Wellness allowance
49.1. Each plan year you may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
49.2. The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

50. Reasonable precautions
50.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
50.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

51. Recovery of costs
51.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

52. Making a claim
52.1. You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
52.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
52.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

53. Arbitration
53.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
53.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

54. Inflation
54.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
54.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

55. Communication
55.1. We will communicate with you in English.
55.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

56. Interest
56.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

57. Dependants
57.1. You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
57.2. Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

58. Notices
58.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
58.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.5. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.6. Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
1.7. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.8. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.9. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.10. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.11. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.12. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.13. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.14. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.15. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.16. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.17. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Interpretation
3.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
3.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
3.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

4. Assignment
4.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

5. Currency
5.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
5.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

6. How to read this document
6.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
6.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
6.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

7. Salvage
7.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
7.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

8. Premium payment
8.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
8.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

9. Replacement devices
9.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
9.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
9.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

10. Geographical limits
10.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
10.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

11. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
11.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
11.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
11.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
11.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
11.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

12. Notices
12.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
12.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

13. Accidental Damage
13.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
13.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
13.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
13.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
13.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

14. Automatic renewal
14.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
14.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

15. Sanctions
15.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

16. Accessibility
16.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

17. Data protection
17.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
17.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
17.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

18. Data and backups
18.1. We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
18.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

19. Instalment agreements
19.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
19.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

20. Compensation scheme
20.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
20.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

21. Claims documents
21.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
21.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

22. Taxes
22.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
22.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

23. Changes in circumstances
23.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
23.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

24. Cancellation
24.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
24.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
24.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

25. Transferring the plan
25.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
25.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

26. Communication
26.1. We will communicate with you in English.
26.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

27. Complaints
27.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
27.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
27.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

28. Unrecoverable devices
28.1. If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
28.2. We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

29. Exchange of information
29.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
29.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

30. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
30.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

31. Fraud
31.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
31.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

32. Payment of claims
32.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
32.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

33. Breakdown
33.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
33.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
33.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
33.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
33.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

34. Recovery of costs
34.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

35. Reasonable precautions
35.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
35.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

36. Other insurance
36.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
36.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

37. General exclusions
37.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
37.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
37.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
37.4. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

38. Software support
38.1. Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
38.2. Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

39. Subrogation
39.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
39.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

40. Waiver
40.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

41. Renewal
41.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
41.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

42. Cooperation
42.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
42.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

43. Electronic documents
43.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
43.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
43.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

44. Customer support
44.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
44.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

45. Governing law
45.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
45.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

46. Market conditions
46.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

47. Joint policyholders
47.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
47.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

48. Inflation
48.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
48.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

49. Making a claim
49.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
49.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
49.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

50. Interest
50.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

51. Environmental commitment
51.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
51.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

52. Third-party administrators
52.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
52.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

53. Severability
53.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

54. Change of address
54.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
54.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

55. Duty of fair presentation
55.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
55.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
55.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

56. Repair process
56.1. After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
56.2. We aim to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

57. Arbitration
57.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
57.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

58. Records and evidence
58.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
58.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
58.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

59. Discounts
59.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
59.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

1. Definitions
1.1. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
1.3. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.4. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.5. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.6. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.7. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.8. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Emergency Medical Expenses
3.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
4.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
5.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

7. Making a claim
7.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.2. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

8. Records and evidence
8.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
8.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
8.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

9. Interest
9.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

10. Cancellation
10.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
10.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
10.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

11. Assignment
11.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

12. Personal liability
12.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
12.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
12.3. The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

13. Emergency assistance
13.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
13.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
13.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

14. Severability
14.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

15. Renewal
15.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
15.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

16. Arbitration
16.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
16.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

17. Environmental commitment
17.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
17.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

18. Customer support
18.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
18.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

19. Legal expenses abroad
19.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
19.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

20. Geographical limits
20.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
20.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

21. Cooperation
21.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
21.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

22. Third-party administrators
22.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
22.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

23. Accessibility
23.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

24. Recovery of costs
24.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

25. Discounts
25.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
25.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.5. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.6. Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
1.7. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.8. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.9. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.10. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
1.11. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.12. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.13. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.14. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.15. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.16. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.17. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
3.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
3.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
3.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

4. Changes in circumstances
4.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
4.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

5. Recovery of costs
5.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

6. Premium payment
6.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
6.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

7. Transferring the plan
7.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
7.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

8. Breakdown
8.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
8.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
8.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
8.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
8.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

9. Communication
9.1. We will communicate with you in English.
9.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

10. Joint policyholders
10.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
10.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

11. Repair process
11.1. After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
11.2. We aim to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

12. Customer support
12.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
12.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

13. Geographical limits
13.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
13.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

14. Cancellation
14.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
14.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
14.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

15. Instalment agreements
15.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
15.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

16. Waiver
16.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

17. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
17.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

18. Duty of fair presentation
18.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
18.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
18.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

19. Notices
19.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
19.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

20. Data and backups
20.1. We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
20.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

21. Replacement devices
21.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
21.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
21.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

22. Interest
22.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

23. Renewal
23.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
23.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

24. Fraud
24.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
24.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

25. Accidental Damage
25.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
25.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
25.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
25.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
25.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

26. Reasonable precautions
26.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
26.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

27. General exclusions
27.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
27.2. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
27.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
27.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
27.5. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

28. Making a claim
28.1. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
28.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
28.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

4.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.

5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
5.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

6. Theft
6.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
6.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
6.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
6.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
6.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
6.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

8. Making a claim
8.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

9. Reasonable precautions
9.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
9.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

10. Electronic documents
10.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
10.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
10.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

11. Exchange of information
11.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
11.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

12. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
12.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

13. Discounts
13.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
13.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

14. Third-party administrators
14.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
14.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

15. Automatic renewal
15.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
15.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

16. Interest
16.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

17. Renewal
17.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
17.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

18. Payment of claims
18.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
18.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

19. Joint policyholders
19.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
19.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

20. Other insurance
20.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
20.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

21. Data protection
21.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
21.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
21.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

22. Alternative accommodation
22.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
22.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
22.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

23. Records and evidence
23.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
23.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
23.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

24. Assignment
24.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

25. Complaints
25.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
25.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
25.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

27. Cooperation
27.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
27.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

28. Taxes
28.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
28.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

32. Changes in circumstances
32.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
32.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

34.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

38.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

39. Change of address

50.2. We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

51. Recovery of costs

52.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

53.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
53.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
53.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

55. Waiver
55.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

56. Salvage
56.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
56.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

57. Instalment agreements
57.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
57.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

58. Contents temporarily removed
58.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
58.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

59. Locks and keys
